summary: Agency trader T-X1005-05 placed a 21768 ICEBERG BUY at 10002 (about 9x top-5 depth). 5835 of it executed in slices over 15:08:57-15:09:09. At 15:09:16 the trader sold 544 at 10006 through a separate LIMIT order (parent B). That sell filled at 15:09:18, and the remaining 15933 of the BUY was cancelled 2s later. The touch had moved +3 ticks and the round trip is +4 ticks. The iceberg and the partial fills give a partial genuine-execution story, but the large unexecuted remainder was pulled right after a profitable opposite-side fill. The evidence is mixed, so I propose escalation to Level 2. This is a single cycle, so I am not proposing a STOR draft.

Registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at its typical size (2464) at or next to the touch, re-quoting as a pair every ~2s. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.963) and follow the mid. The BUY/SELL 'opposite' fills were executions on the trader's own resting quotes; price did not move in the trader's favour (price_move 0.0, reversion 0.0) and the round trip is negative (-0.19 ticks). Neither core feature is present; market making is supported. Level 2 may review.

PROP-EQ trader (no MM registration) placed a single BUY of 18,930 (7.9x top-5 depth) 1 tick below the bid and cancelled it after 803 ms with no fills of any kind. Feature (b), a benefit from an opposite-side execution, is absent. Feature (a), an order not meant to execute, is plausible (size ~38x the trader's typical 500, quick cancel, a 1,893 re-entry at the same price 1.2 s later) and no accepted legitimate explanation is supported. Evidence is mixed, so it goes to Level 2 under the escalation standard. It is not a STOR draft: there is no benefit, no repetition and no prior alerts.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A refreshing a two-sided 356-lot quote every 1-6s, re-posting within ~25ms of each cancel at levels that track the touch. Cancels are almost perfectly symmetric across sides (0.99). The detector's 'opposite-side execution' (SELL 143 at 10003) was a fill on the trader's own resting SELL quote, which sat at the touch. The price moved against the trader (-1 tick) and did not revert after the cancels. No evidence of an order meant not to execute, and no spoofing-type benefit. The detector's size trigger comes from summing continual quote refreshes (gross 8900 in 60s), not from any single large order. Caveat for L2: round_trip_ticks is +2.59, consistent with market-maker spread capture but positive.

Detector fired on large gross submission and cancels after opposite-side fills. The tape shows a PEGGED two-sided execution algo: 76 pegged orders, all children of parents P-T-X1012-02-B/-S, 2424 per order (desk typical size), at the touch, cancelled and re-pegged symmetrically with the touch (symmetry 0.996). Fills on both sides were genuine executions of the resting orders (same-side 1708). No favourable move with reversion, no event, no repeated spoof cycle. The only soft point is a small positive round trip (1.41 ticks), consistent with spread capture by a two-sided algo rather than price pushing.

Prop trader placed two BUY limits of 7215 each (14430 total, 5.5x avg top-5 depth, ~1.5 ticks from touch, 1 level) at 15:12:52.998 and 15:12:55.998. At 15:13:20.498 a 515 SELL filled at 10001 after the bid had risen 1.5 ticks. Both BUYs were cancelled at 15:13:23.140, 142 ms after an unscheduled issuer news item (15:13:22.998). The news timing is a candidate explanation, but the sale preceded the news and followed a favourable move, and nothing shows the BUYs were a genuine attempt to buy. Evidence is mixed, so escalate to Level 2. This is not a STOR draft: there is no repetition in the session and no prior alerts.
